scope: Restore the full Nanobrowser agent in the default Xroga extension and add a local Chrome execution target using canonical browser run records, leases, and metered DeepSeek dispatch.

keep: Nanobrowser browser control, task loop, scoped tabs and recovery journal
Existing Xroga account, model ledger, browser run and lease stores
extend: Same-tab authenticated Workspace pairing and task controls
Chrome-local action visualization and model turn adapter
replace: The limited page-reading default extension build

schemaImpact.rollout: Apply the shared pacing expansion with legacy defaults before enabling a verified key pilot. Local Chrome run limits and usage use the existing state JSON. Activate only on compatible frontend and API releases.
schemaImpact.rollback: Restore the previous per-key interval and concurrency without clearing leases or ledger entries. Disable the local Chrome API flag and Workspace extension ID to stop new local runs.

auth.description: Workspace verifies an existing account before pairing and authenticates each API request. The browser service worker never holds the account bearer.

tenant.description: Local browser runs, turn claims and result writes are owner scoped. The extension requires separate Chrome profiles for different Xroga accounts.

approval.description: The extension retains the upstream user handover and requires one-off approval for classified writes without automatic site allowance.

credentials.description: Xroga uses the existing platform model credential on the server.

egress.description: A paired Workspace tab relays bounded model turns through the authenticated Xroga API. The server rejects image, secret-bearing and oversized context.

cost.description: The enabled feature can spend through the existing provider ledger. Run and turn caps bound the route. Fixture tests spend zero.

billing.description: The existing ledger admits and settles platform-funded Zurelay requests. The task allowance uses the same receipt calculation and retains the full per-turn ceiling when the charge is unknown.

tests.scope: Passed in Chrome 156 with a deterministic model. Verified both entry points, real navigation, a single-field GET form that needed one-time approval, and a stopped pending turn.
The isolated Chrome probe uses the exact live Zurelay model with a synthetic site and Workspace bridge. Hosted authentication and settlement are separate acceptance requirements.
Canonical owner binding, hosted recovery exclusion, input refusal, replay rejection and cancellation.

architecture.reason: Local Chrome uses the existing browser run records, execution leases and metered model dispatch, and hosted recovery skips this execution target.

rollout: Keep the product disabled until integrated release gates and genuine model acceptance pass.
rollback: Disable the feature flags and disconnect or remove the extension.
knownGaps: Authenticated staging with live ledger settlement, multi-user Chrome acceptance, and approved live website workflows are pending.
Model vision remains disabled for browser tasks until this exact route passes privacy and modality acceptance.
Explicit resume preserves the same run ID, time and spend on the paired device. A full Chrome restart and re-pair still needs live acceptance.
The repository-wide mission check inherits a stale voice mission ancestry reference.

blockers: Authenticated hosted staging, hosted settlement reconciliation, browser restart acceptance, site-specific outcomes, and source-pinned release approval.
